transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nikhil Rao (Redwood), Priya Kapoor (NovaSearch Head of Search), Liam O'Neill (NovaSearch ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Infra Lead), Alex Tan (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, imperfect):
NovaSearch is evaluating Redwood for a rerank/embedding pipeline. Primary concerns: vector dimensionality tradeoffs (cost vs quality), batching and KV-cache effect on latency SLOs, quantization impact on vector similarity, and VPC/on-prem networking + KMS for private data. Action: run benchmarks with three dimension configs and three batch sizes; Redwood to share quantization docs and provide pricing for Dedicated and Private deployment.

Topics: vector dims, batch sizing, KV cache for rerank, quantization (int8/4-bit), VPC/on-prem networking and KMS, benchmark plan, costing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro: I'm Maya, AE for the account, Diego is our SE, Nikhil's here for any systems questions. Priya, do you want to kick off with the high level ask?
[00:14] Priya: Yeah, thanks. We're trying to firm up how we take our current two-stage search + rerank into production. We care about top-5 rerank latency under 120ms p95 and cost per query. Also privacy — we need VPC or on-prem option for certain regs.
[00:29] Diego: cool, so we'll cover model dims, batching, kv cache, and then the private deploy bits. quick clarifying q: is your current embedding dim 768 or are you already experimenting with 1536?
[00:41] Liam: right now prod is 384 for recall stage and 1536 for reranker embeddings, but it's expensive. we're exploring 128/384 for rerank to see tradeoffs.
[00:53] Nikhil: and what throughput are you aiming for? qps, concurrency?
[00:58] Alex: baseline is ~200 qps sustained, spikes to 800 qps during peak, typical query distribution is 70% short queries, 30% long context + user metadata.
[01:12] Diego: ok noted. for throughput and latency, batching is the lever — but it interacts with latency SLO. smaller batch => lower p95 but worse GPU utilization (higher unit cost). larger batch => better tokens/sec but adds batch latency.
[01:31] Priya: can you quantify? like if we go 128 dim vs 1536 and batch sizes 1,8,32 what should we expect p95-wise?
[01:40] Diego: rough numbers from past runs: on a gpus similar to A10/A30 we see —
[01:45] Diego: 1536 dim, batch=1 -> ~40-60ms per vector forward (rerank-only model), batch=8 -> amortized 18-25ms per vector but added tail due to batching wait; batch=32 -> 8-12ms amortized but cold-start + queueing can push p95 higher if qps variable.
[02:03] Diego: 384 dim is ~0.25x compute of 1536 so numbers drop accordingly, 128 dim is tiny, like 3-6ms at batch=1 and sub-ms amortized at large batches, but quality delta matters.
[02:18] Liam: that aligns with intuition. our quality team will want A/B tests but we need a cost envelope.
[02:25] Maya: worth calling out KV cache — for rerank workflows where many requests share prefixes (e.g., same document context or same session), Redwood's prefix + KV cache can sidestep repeated compute for the prefix and only run cross-attention on new tokens. That can dramatically lower per-query latency.
[02:44] Priya: is k/v cache applicable for embeddings/rerank? I thought kv cache was for generation.
[02:50] Diego: correct, it's mostly for autoregressive models, but for embedding-based rerank we use a similar concept: cached encodings for candidate passages or re-used context embeddings. For example, maintain a cache of passage embeddings and lookups avoid recompute. The other half is query encoding which is cheap. Important to distinguish: if your rerank model does cross-encoder scoring (concat query+doc) then caching doc-side encodings is possible if we use dual-encoder -> simpler; cross-encoder may need full forward.
[03:21] Sofia: our current rerank is cross-encoder, so caching docs won't fully avoid the model compute, but we can cache first-pass features.
[03:28] Diego: right, so options: migrate to dual-encoder + fast dot product for initial scoring then cross-encoder for top-k (small k) — Redwood supports hybrid flows and can orchestrate fallback to cross-encoder when needed. That saves compute because cross-encoder is applied to a handful of candidates.
[03:48] Priya: okay good. in that hybrid setup what are batch tradeoffs? If we send top-50 candidates and run cross-encoder on 200 queries/sec, batching those 50*200 workloads seems large.
[03:59] Diego: you usually batch at the cross-encoder call granularity. For top-50 per query at 200 qps that's 10k forward ops per second. We recommend either increase the early prune to top-10 for production or use sharded workers with dedicated GPU pools; Redwood Dedicated can reserve capacity for consistent p95 SLOs.
[04:19] Nikhil: another angle is vector dimensionality reduction + PCA/OPQ or product quantization for index speed; then run cross-encoder on smaller candidate set. That reduces index memory and nearest neighbor cost.
[04:31] Liam: about quantization: we've been experimenting with int8 and 4-bit quant for embeddings — what's Redwood's experience on quality delta for rerank?
[04:40] Diego: quant for the model weights often keeps generation quality pretty close for int8; 4-bit can be trickier but is good with calibrated quantization and per-channel scales. For embeddings specifically, vector quantization (PQ/OPQ) for indices is different than weight quant; PQ will add some nearest-neighbor recall loss. Our internal tests show 384-dim with PQ (64-subvectors, 8 bits) retains ~95% recall for top-50 in many corpora, but it's dataset dependent.
[05:09] Priya: so we need to run our own eval. we'll supply some telemetry and relevance labels.
[05:15] Maya: perfect. operationally, on the Private/VPC side: Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC with a control plane that can be hosted or self-managed — network egress, KMS integration, and audit logs are available. Diego, can you expand on auth & KMS?
[05:31] Diego: yes. for VPC we offer customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault), or you can bring an HSM. Keys never leave your KMS; the inference nodes request short-lived wrapping tokens. Audit logs are shipped to your S3 or logging endpoint. For on-prem air-gapped setups we provide an offline installer and a local control plane option.
[05:50] Sofia: with VPC/on-prem we worry about latencies between app tier and model tier — if the model sits in another AZ or private colo, that can add RTT. what's the typical network add-on?
[05:59] Nikhil: within same region AZ it's a few ms; cross-region is larger. For strict 120ms p95 it's usually fine, but if you have 50ms budget for rerank you want colocated model pools. For on-prem, we'd advise deploying the model in the same network as the serving frontends. Redwood's Dedicated can be provisioned in customer region or colocations via partner.
[06:21] Alex: cost — do you have ballparks for Dedicated GPU pools sized for our 800 qps spikes with a hybrid approach?
[06:29] Maya: we'll put together a sizing estimate, but a rough sketch: if cross-encoder at 1536 dims is used for top-10 at 800 qps, you'll need multiple GPUs to avoid queuing. The exact number depends on batch tuning and reserved concurrency; we'll run workload sims.
[06:42] Liam: can we run a bench where we vary dims (128/384/1536) and batch 1/8/32 with and without KV/idx PQ? we want latency p50/p95 and recall metrics.
[06:52] Diego: yes — action item. We'll set up a harness that runs permutations and returns p50/p95 p99 and recall@k against your labels. Any constraints for data sharing?
[07:01] Priya: we can provide anonymized docs and 1k labeled queries; need NDA though for some corpora.
[07:07] Maya: we have NDA on file; we'll make sure bench runs under isolation rules for Private if needed.
[07:12] Diego: a few gotchas to call out: 1) batching period adds latency jitter — we can use dynamic batching to cap latency with a max batch wait, 2) KV cache requires cache warm-up; cold-start results look worse, 3) quantized model loading can take slightly longer during cold start if we stream kernels.
[07:34] Priya: what about warm vs cold calls? during peak we should be warm but at night we'll have cold restarts.
[07:39] Nikhil: we'll instrument with warm pools and keep a small always-on reserved capacity in Dedicated to avoid cold start. Redwood can do micro-autoscale with min nodes.
[07:49] Liam: any caution around aggregation of embeddings in 128 dim causing collisions, especially with PQ?
[07:55] Diego: yes, lower dims compress semantic space; more collisions risk and recall drops. That's why we recommend A/Bing dims on your labeled set — often 384 is a sweet spot between cost and recall for many web corpora, but domain-specific corpora like legal or medical may need 1536.
[08:13] Priya: notes on eval design — we want recall@10, MRR, and latency p95.
[08:19] Maya: noted. we'll include those metrics.
[08:22] Alex: security question: if we choose Private, who manages patching and runtime updates?
[08:27] Diego: for Private with customer-managed control plane you manage the infra but Redwood provides container images and patch bundles. For fully-managed Private we handle patch orchestration under an agreed maintenance window.
[08:40] Sofia: do you have SOC 2 / ISO artifacts?
[08:43] Maya: yes — we'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs; also CA certificates and network diagrams.
[08:49] Priya: excellent. back to quantization — do you recommend doing quant on the index (PQ) or model weights? our current plan was PQ on the index to save memory, then int8 for weights to reduce VM size.
[09:00] Diego: that strategy makes sense. PQ for index reduces memory consumption and ANN latency, weight quant reduces serving memory and can increase throughput by fitting larger batch on-device. We will provide int8 tested images and guidance for calibration.
[09:12] Liam: do you have numbers for cost reduction if we go int8 + PQ vs full fp16?
[09:18] Diego: ballpark: int8 weight quant may give 1.5x-2x throughput improvement depending on kernel support; PQ index can reduce storage by 4-8x and ANN search latency improves accordingly. Combined, unit cost per query could drop 2-4x — highly workload dependent. We'll quantify in benchmarks.
[09:38] Priya: what's the timeline to get bench artifacts?
[09:41] Maya: we'll aim to have initial bench results in 7 business days after we get the 1k queries and dataset. Longer 48h stress tests will follow.
[09:50] Alex: for the POC, we want a VPC private deployment with customer KMS and an isolated Dedicated GPU pool. Can Redwood support an initial 30-day eval?
[09:59] Maya: yes, we typically do a 30-day POC — Diego will own the technical setup and we'll put together a SOW for the POC scope.
[10:08] Diego: technical detail: for VPC we recommend colocating the GPU pool in your VPC via PrivateLink or by spinning up a VPC-peered subnet in our infra; either way we support TLS + mutual auth. For on-prem, we'll provide an installer and offline images.
[10:26] Sofia: curious on telemetry — can we keep logs on our side? we want the model traces and per-token timing.
[10:32] Nikhil: yes, Redwood Console can stream traces and we can push to your logging endpoint. For Private, logs remain in your plumbing.
[10:41] Priya: edge case: we have some PII in doc corpus — need redaction and strict retention.
[10:46] Maya: noted. Redwood supports configurable retention and redaction pipelines; we'll include options in the security checklist.
[10:53] Liam: are there any known stability issues with sustained PQ + quant workloads?
[10:58] Diego: not major, but you should watch for index rebuilds and background GC that can spike I/O — we recommend staggering background jobs and monitoring disk IOPS. We'll include best-practices.
[11:12] Priya: ok let's recap next steps.
[11:15] Maya: recap: 1) NovaSearch sends 1k labeled queries + sample docs and query distribution (Liam). 2) Diego builds benchmark harness for dims [128,384,1536], batch sizes [1,8,32], PQ on/off, quant int8/4-bit on/off, returns latency + recall metrics (Diego). 3) Redwood sends quant docs, SOC2/ISO pack, VPC diagram, and pricing draft (Maya). 4) Schedule POC kickoff the week of Dec 1 once NDA and data are in place (everyone).
[11:46] Priya: yep that works. any open questions?
[11:50] Alex: one: can we run the bench in our cloud account to measure network effects?
[11:55] Diego: yes — we can run the load generator from your VPC against Redwood Dedicated in your region or from within your account if we deploy the model there. We'll coordinate infra details in the action item.
[12:06] Maya: ok wrapping — thanks all. Diego, any final notes?
[12:10] Diego: just that we'll include a config file template for the bench so you can tweak k and batching windows. watch out for warm pools and max batch wait parameter.
[12:20] Priya: great. thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
